observations: body L2, L4-L6, L8, L18, L26, L32, L38: the dashes of «al–Battānī» are long dashes (5.3 to 5.6 pt); in L18, L26, L32 and L38 the name is letter-spaced.

body L8-L10, L12, L20, L27-L29, L39, L41-L42: the dashes of 9.6 to 10.4 pt, after the head letters and before the names, are transcribed as dashes, as that before «Schiaparelli» in L39, which prints 7.4 pt long; those of «1–4», «4–5» and «9–11» in the heads are long dashes.
body L10: 42° and 52° are the true longitudes of the Sun less the apogee: 124° 1′ 32″ − 82° 17′ 42″ = 41° 43′ 50″ (p. 230) and 134° 36′ 13″ − 82° 33′ 12″ = 52° 3′ 1″ (p. 231).

body L11-L19: AL = 5p,247 is 60p sin 5° 1′, al-Battānī's greatest equation of the Moon (p. 221). In the triangle AEL the angle at A is 180° less QAL; with QAL 114° 16′ and 111° 4′, EL is 58p,0407 and 58p,3199, and 60p less these 1p,96 and 1p,68; with the true anomalies of pp. 230 and 231, 114° 13′ 38″ and 111° 9′ 1″, EL would be 58p,044 and 58p,312.
body (figure): the figure is not drawn to scale: AL is about an eighth of AE, where 5p,247 to 60p is about an eleventh, and the angle QAL is about 112°.

body L20-L27: 0° 31′ 52″ is the latitude of p. 230, and 0° 28′ 3″ the latitude that al-Battānī's table gives for the eclipse IV (p. 231, where the computation prints 0° 28′ 9″); 31′ 52″ − 28′ 3″ = 3′ 49″. The motion in latitude 185° 21′ is that of the codex in the table of p. 232.
body L29-L36: 8 3/4 × 3′ 50″ = 33′ 32 1/2″, the diameter of 33′ 1/2 of L36; 6 × 3′ 50″ = 23′ (L32). The bar of «1 − 5/6» in L31 (10.2 pt) is a minus sign.
